objects: Analyze this ARC-AGI-3 game-state image and return only valid SWI-Prolog source code, with no Markdown fences and no prose. Friendly semantic object names are the permanent canonical IDs from the beginning of the level to the end. At the top, emit exactly one object_identity(ObjectId, Type, Label) fact for every visible object, one fact per line. ObjectId must be a descriptive lowercase snake_case atom such as blue_player, red_goal, left_wall, yellow_key, moving_platform, or blue_square_2. Never use opaque IDs such as obj_1, object_2, item_3, or shape_4. Reuse every supplied existing ObjectId exactly when it denotes the same object. Never rename, recycle, or silently replace an existing ID. Create a new friendly name only for a truly new object. Then describe each visible object with bounding boxes, colors, geometry, containment, adjacency, state, and other useful properties. Every fact referring to an object must use its canonical friendly ObjectId. For each drawable object, include turtle_program(ObjectId, Program) using Turtle DSL instructions such as penup, pendown, set_pos(X,Y), setcolor(Color), set_cell, fwd(N), and rot(Degrees). Rotations are relative. Keep coordinates explicit and preserve the rendered state exactly. Detect useful object structure at multiple granularities: whole semantic objects, contiguous color blobs, rectangular blocks, line segments, bars, holes or enclosures, useful sub-objects, and compound block structures. Do not omit block objects merely because they are parts of a larger semantic object.
differences: Compare the previous and current ARC-AGI-3 states and return only valid SWI-Prolog source code. Use the canonical friendly object names from object_registry.pl and the supplied objects.pl files exactly. Never introduce substitute IDs. Write differences suitable for differences.pl, including added_object/1, removed_object/1, changed_object/3, moved_object/4, recolored_object/3, resized_object/3, unchanged_object/2, action_effect/2, and other useful predicates. A newly observed object may receive a new friendly name only if it is genuinely absent from the registry. Distinguish observation from hypothesis.
redraw: Return only valid SWI-Prolog source. Generate Turtle DSL facts that redraw the current ARC-AGI-3 image faithfully. Use the canonical friendly ObjectIds from object_registry.pl and objects.pl for every turtle_program/2 or object reference. Never rename objects or invent opaque IDs.
redraw_diff: Return only valid SWI-Prolog source. Generate a Turtle DSL patch transforming the previous state into the current state using the smallest clear operations. Use the canonical friendly ObjectIds from object_registry.pl, parent objects.pl, current objects.pl, and differences.pl. Never rename or replace IDs.
similarity: Return only valid SWI-Prolog source. Match objects between the previous and current ARC-AGI-3 states using the canonical friendly ObjectIds. Include object_match/3 facts with confidence and evidence, plus unmatched objects. The same persistent object must use the same friendly name on both sides; do not generate new aliases or opaque IDs.
bootstrap_identities: Inspect the initial ARC-AGI-3 level image and assign permanent friendly semantic names. Return only a JSON object with one key named objects whose value is an array. Each array item must contain id, type, and label strings, and may contain color. The id must be descriptive lowercase snake_case, such as blue_player, red_goal, left_wall, top_bar_segment, or yellow_block_cluster. Never use obj_1, object_2, shape_3, or other opaque numbering. Include meaningful whole objects and useful block-level objects: contiguous color blobs, rectangles, bars, line segments, holes, enclosures, useful sub-objects, and compound block structures. Do not return Markdown or Prolog.
repair_identities: Normalize the candidate analysis into strict JSON only. Return {"objects":[...]} where each item contains id, type, and label strings. Use friendly descriptive lowercase snake_case ids. Include all visible semantic and useful block-level objects. Never use opaque ids such as obj_1 or shape_2.
repair_objects: Repair the candidate into valid SWI-Prolog only, with no Markdown or prose. Begin with exactly one object_identity(ObjectId, Type, Label) fact for every visible object. Reuse the canonical friendly IDs from the supplied object_registry.pl exactly. Then retain or reconstruct object properties and turtle_program/2 facts. Track semantic objects and useful block-level structures.
rules: Return only valid SWI-Prolog source. Infer cautious hypothetical transition rules for the current ARC3 state and action path. Use canonical friendly ObjectIds exactly. Separate observed_rule/2 from hypothetical_rule/3 and include evidence references. Use current objects.pl, differences.pl, action history, and object registry. Do not rename objects.
